howto.name: Upload GIF images
howto.text: Drop one or many .gif files. Animated GIFs use only the first frame.

howto.name: Choose page size
howto.text: Auto (the default) makes each page the size of its GIF; Letter or A4 scale each GIF to fit while preserving aspect ratio.

howto.name: Download the PDF
howto.text: All GIFs are combined into one PDF, one image per page in upload order. Only the pixels are copied, so comments, location and camera details in the files do not go into the PDF.

faq.q: Do animated GIFs animate inside the PDF?
faq.a: No — PDF doesn't support animation. Only the first frame is used. To convert animation to PDF, use GIF to MP4 and then Video to PDF, which lays out evenly spaced frames, one per page.

It is not kept. Transparent pixels show the colour stored in their palette entry, which is often black, and PNG to PDF does not keep transparency either. Flatten the GIF onto a white background first if needed.

faq.q: Can the GIF stay as a GIF inside the PDF?
faq.a: No. PDF has no GIF image type, so the first frame is decoded and stored with lossless Flate compression; no JPEG step is involved.
